summary:
M5 (monthly update form, C3/C6, on-behalf entry) is built and all my checks pass. I couldn't click through it in a browser: signing in needs 2FA and I must not touch .env.local. To make up for that, a test renders the whole form on the server in every mode and checks what each audience sees.

What it does:
- **List page, /portal/[companyId]/updates:** every month with its status badge (red "Overdue" variant plus days late), due date (and "extended from"), narrative filled / not yet / skipped, and open comment count. A main button jumps to the earliest month that still needs work ("Start", "Continue" or "Make changes <Month>"). A note says months are submitted in order (B5). Empty states cover "Not yet reporting" (no start month) and a first month that hasn't opened yet, and there is a read-only notice for exited companies. The page calls open_due_periods on load and only logs a failure. Phones get cards, desktops a table.
- **Company form page, /portal/[companyId]/updates/[month]:** the month is parsed with parseMonthKey (anything else is a 404, and a full date redirects to the YYYY-MM URL). Mode is "company" when canEnterData(ctx, companyId, company.status) is true and the month is a draft or sent back; otherwise "readonly". canSubmit comes from canSubmit(ctx, companyId). Comment counts are worked out on the server from the threads the viewer can see.
- **ScaleUp form page, /admin/companies/[companyId]/updates/[month]:** Fund Admins get "on_behalf" mode with the banner "You are entering data on behalf of <Company>. Changes are logged."; every other ScaleUp role gets a read-only "View only" view. Submit is never shown there, and the header has "Open review page" linking to /admin/review/<submissionId>.
- **The form itself:**
  - A sticky bar shows the month, status, due date or overdue, the save state ("Saving…", "Saved 14:05", "Couldn't save · Retry"), a Comments button with the unresolved count that opens the threads panel in a side sheet, and "Review and submit". Contributors see "Only your company owner can submit this month." instead.
  - Status banners cover changes requested (the latest message), awaiting review, approved and locked (with "Request amendment" for owners, which asks for a reason), read-only companies, on-behalf entry, and earlier months still to submit (with links).
  - Sections follow the template order:
    - **Financials:** revenue by active segment with a read-only live total (or a plain total-revenue box when there are no segments), then the other four figures including the "Enter 0 if cash-flow positive" hint, and last month's figure under each box.
    - **Live metrics:** gross margin, net margin, runway and revenue change against last month.
    - **Headcount.**
    - **KPI grid:** a table per dimension (e.g. outlets by KPI) plus plain fields for the other KPIs, with the right input for each value type.
    - **Additional-number sections.**
    - **Narrative:** accordions per C4 category, each field with a "Last month" section and "Copy last month" (it asks before overwriting).
    - **Founder pulse:** 1–5 morale buttons labelled from the template, goals, help needed and help tags.
  - Numbers are typed into text boxes with a decimal keypad, show the currency symbol, and are reformatted when you leave the box. Text that can't be read as a number stays on screen with a message and is not saved.
  - Inline errors appear once a field has been left or after the first submit attempt. A "Before this month can be submitted" panel lists every problem with a link to the field.
  - Read-only mode shows plain text, with no inputs.
- **Review and submit:** it saves pending changes, runs the server check (earlier months are listed with links, other problems with jump links), shows the figures actually stored with the declaration text and a tick box, then submits. On success it shows a toast and goes to the list.
- **Autosave:** it waits about 1.2 s after the last change, sends only what changed, and never runs two saves at once. If a save fails the changes are kept and can be retried. It saves when the tab is hidden or you leave the page, and warns before closing the tab with unsaved changes. Figures a co-worker saved meanwhile replace fields you haven't touched, and a page rendered before your latest save can't overwrite what you typed.
- **Server actions (src/lib/actions/submission.ts):** saveSubmissionValues, getSubmissionValidationAction, submitSubmission and requestAmendment. Saving is for members of the company or a Fund Admin; submitting and amendments are owner-only. Each validates its input with zod, turns database errors into friendly messages, and refreshes the affected pages.
deviations: SubmissionForm gained two optional props (§5.7 allows this): canStartThreads?: boolean (default false; pass canComment(ctx) on ScaleUp pages) and earlierDrafts?: string[] (YYYY-MM months still in draft, shown as a 'Submit … first' warning). The exported names and existing props are unchanged.

saveSubmissionValues revalidates on every autosave, as the brief asks. In Next 16 that means each save's response also re-renders the current form page, roughly one page render (about 20 queries) per save. I kept it because it keeps the form current (co-workers' figures fill untouched fields) and clears the back/forward cache, so pressing Back never shows old figures. I checked the Next source: a same-URL revalidation doesn't scroll and replaces the history entry. If it proves too chatty, remove the revalidatePath calls in saveSubmissionValues only.

getSubmissionValidationAction returns more than the RPC: { ok, errors, priorMonths (YYYY-MM, queried only when the prior_months rule fails), values (stored value columns only), lastSavedAt, status }, so the declaration step shows exactly what is stored. It is read-only, so it revalidates nothing.
saveSubmissionValues returns { savedAt: string | null }; null only for an empty payload, which never calls the RPC.

After a successful submit the form toasts and calls router.push('/portal/<id>/updates') without an extra router.refresh(). submitSubmission's revalidatePath already re-renders the page and clears the client router cache, so the list loads fresh.

Company users only get a FieldCommentButton on fields, segments and KPI cells that already have threads (they can't start threads). ScaleUp staff get one on every target when canStartThreads is true, otherwise only where threads exist.

Extra paths revalidated: /admin/companies/<id>/updates/<month> and /admin/review/<submissionId> by every action; also /portal/<id>/history and /admin/companies/<id> after submit and amendment requests.

Numbers are rounded as typed to what the database stores (4 decimals; revenue segments 2), half away from zero like Postgres numeric, so the screen matches the stored value. Whole-number KPIs refuse decimals in the input rather than saving them, because the RPC rejects the whole save batch otherwise. Whole-number template fields such as headcount are saved and flagged by validation, as the contract says.

With revenue segments, total revenue is the live sum of the active segments and is saved automatically. When the form opens and the stored total differs from the sum (e.g. a segment was deactivated) and at least one segment has an amount, the total is corrected and autosaved.

Extras: not-found.tsx and error.tsx for my routes; a 'View only' banner for ScaleUp roles other than Fund Admin on draft or sent-back months; a non-canonical month parameter (e.g. 2026-09-15) redirects to the YYYY-MM URL; the list page calls open_due_periods() on load and logs rather than shows any error.
openQuestions: Autosave re-renders the form page on every save (revalidatePath in saveSubmissionValues, per the brief). Is that cost acceptable, or should autosave skip revalidation and only submit and amendment revalidate? The trade-off is described in the deviations.
Months can be filled in while an earlier month is still a draft; only submitting is blocked, and a warning banner links to the earlier months. Confirm that editing ahead should stay allowed.
An owner can request another amendment while one is still pending (the button then reads 'Request another amendment'). Should that be blocked until ScaleUp reopens or answers?
The Comments button shows for company users even when there are no threads (it opens an empty panel). Hide it when there are none?
The monthly updates list calls open_due_periods() on every load, as §2.4 describes for portal page loads, in addition to M7's home page call. Keep both?
notesForOtherModules:
Routes exposed by M5:
- /portal/[companyId]/updates: the monthly updates list.
- /portal/[companyId]/updates/[month]: the company form, month as YYYY-MM.
- /admin/companies/[companyId]/updates/[month]: Fund Admin on-behalf entry; read-only for other ScaleUp roles; the header links to /admin/review/<submissionId>.
There is deliberately no /admin/companies/[companyId]/updates list page (not in the brief).

M6 (review and comments), four points:
- Link 'Edit on behalf' to /admin/companies/<companyId>/updates/<YYYY-MM>. Show it when canEnterData(ctx, companyId, company.status) is true and the status is draft or changes_requested.
- The form renders FieldCommentButton with targets field:<key>, segment:<segmentId>, kpi:<kpiId> and kpi:<kpiId>:<memberId> (src/lib/targets.ts), and CommentThreadsPanel with no target inside a right-hand Sheet (SheetContent w-full sm:max-w-md; the panel sits in a scrollable p-4 box). Keep the panel fluid-width.
- Company users only get FieldCommentButton where count >= 1, with canStartThreads=false.
- Comment counts are computed server-side on the form pages (root comments grouped by target; resolved_at null = unresolved). Please revalidatePath('/portal/<companyId>/updates/<YYYY-MM>'), '/admin/companies/<companyId>/updates/<YYYY-MM>' and '/portal/<companyId>/updates' after adding or resolving comments so the counts refresh.

M7 (tracker and home): link the portal home to /portal/<companyId>/updates and /portal/<companyId>/updates/<YYYY-MM>. For a matching call to action, reuse nextActionMonth(rows), actionLabel(row) ('Start' / 'Continue' / 'Make changes') and isEditableStatus from '@/components/submission-form/presentation' (pure and client-safe; rows from listCompanySubmissions).
M1 (companies): the company detail page can link each month to /admin/companies/<companyId>/updates/<YYYY-MM>. That page's not-found state links back to /admin/companies/<companyId>.

Integrator, three points:
- src/components/submission-form/queries.ts is server-only (loadCommentCounts, listEarlierDrafts) and is imported by both form pages and the Server Action.
- Page props are typed explicitly as { params: Promise<{ companyId: string; month: string }> }; run next typegen/build as usual.
- No shared files, config, dependencies or navigation were changed; the portal sidebar already links 'Monthly updates' to /portal/<id>/updates. tests/features/m5 mocks '@/components/comments/comment-threads', so it stays green whatever M6 ships.
